reason: R2 only provides a DC reference/leak path for node net44, which otherwise is only connected to VOUT1 through C0. If you don’t care about net44 having a defined DC voltage (e.g., it’s not probed/used elsewhere), removing R2 won’t change the main amplifier’s signal path.
impact_estimate: Low; net44 becomes a floating node (can affect operating-point convergence or any measurement taken at net44).

reason: C0 forms an auxiliary RC network with R2 involving a side node (net44) that is not otherwise connected to the amplifier core. If the circuit’s intent is primarily DC/low-frequency differential amplification and you don’t need this compensation/filtering path, C0 can be removed with minimal functional change.
impact_estimate: Low-to-moderate; may change transient/AC stability or bandwidth only if that RC was intended as compensation or load modeling.

reason: R3 acts mainly as an explicit output load/bleeder to ground; many amplifier tests don’t require a fixed resistive load, and the output can be left unloaded (or loaded by whatever follows). Removing it typically doesn’t break biasing inside the amplifier because internal devices set the operating point.
impact_estimate: Low-to-moderate; increases output impedance/lightens load, potentially increasing gain and altering output DC level if the design relied on a defined load.
